simple.meaning: תָּאָה (tâʼâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to mark off , i.e. (intensively) designate.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Numbers, beginning at Numbers 34:7. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תָּאָה (H8376) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: תָּאָה (tâʼâh) / H8376 is traced through Numbers 34:7, Numbers 34:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “ ‘This shall be your north border: from the great sea you shall mark out for yourselves Mount Hor.

timeline.evidenceText: “ ‘This shall be your north border: from the great sea you shall mark out for yourselves Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor you shall mark out to the entrance of Hamath; and the border shall pass by Zedad.
